text: I have found the perfect answer to Not All Men. The Chinese girls are cooking because listen to this. Out of 10 men, 1 makes a sexual joke direct at a woman, 2 laugh along, 3 don't find it funny but still chuckle to fit in, 4 say nothing, they pretend they didn't hear it at all, not a single one speaks up, not a single one stops it. Later, aside from the man who made the joke, the other 9 all believe the same thing. Men like that are a minority, most men aren't like this, they all see themselves as part of the good majority. But from the woman's perspective, the one being harassed, there is no big difference between them. The laughter, the silence, the looking away, all of it creates the same environment. So when women say most men are the same, this is what they mean. Not every man harasses women, but that most men participate in protecting the system that does. So let's slow this down for a second and actually look at the logic here. The claim is this. Out of 10 men, 1 makes inappropriate joke, some laugh, some awkwardly chuckle, some stay silent, and nobody speaks up. And the conclusion? Most men are the same. Most men are protecting the system. Here's the problem. That's a moral expansion trick. You take the worst actor in the room, the guy who made the joke, and then you stretch responsibility to everyone present. But silence is not the same as endorsement. There are many reasons why people don't intervene in the moment. Social pressure, fear of escalation, not wanting public conflict, being caught off guard, not knowing what to say. You can criticize passivity, sure, but equating passivity with offensive behavior is a logical leap. Now let's test this logic properly. Imagine, out of 10 men, 1 actually speaks up and shuts it down. What happens then? Do all men suddenly become good? Of course not. So the framework collapses the moment the numbers change. Let's go deeper. Men also created the very systems that restrain bad men. Police, law enforcement, courts. Why do these exist? Because without them, society turns into chaos. Rule of the jungle. The strongest wins. Humans created structures to prevent exactly that. Now follow the same logic. A small percentage of men built legal systems. Some men enforce them. Some support them. Some just comply with them. By this logic, that would mean most men are protecting justice. But that's also false. Which proves the point. Participation in a society does not equal endorsement of every individual's behavior inside it. Now let's flip it. Imagine one woman posts a toxic misandrist video about men. Out of 9 women watching, 2 comment positively. 3 like it to fit in. 4 think it's wrong but stay silent. Does that mean all women are protecting a system of misandry? Of course not. And if you reject that conclusion, you must reject the original one too. Logic has to work both ways. Yes, from an emotional perspective, silence can feel like complicity. That feeling is real. But feelings are not the same as facts. There is a difference between the person who commits harm, the person who actively supports it, and the person who fails to intervene. Those are not identical categories. The moment you collapse them into one, you remove new ones. And when you say most men are the same, you are not encouraging accountability. You are assigning collective guilt. And collective guilt rarely produces improvement. It produces defensiveness. If you want people to speak up more, you encourage courage. You normalize intervention. You reward accountability. You don't tell people they are guilty no matter what they do. Because the moment guilt becomes collective, justice stops being justice. It becomes ideology. And that's the real issue here.
